macro_blurb: Geopolitical risk is front and center for European and US markets today, with the US reporting another soldier killed as the Iran war escalates over the weekend, while Ukrainian drone strikes ignited Russian oil installations—an event with direct implications for crude-linked energy names on both sides of the Atlantic. In the UK, Thames Water lenders are preparing a legal challenge against a potential Burnham-led nationalisation, keeping utility and creditor-rights concerns in focus for European investors. From China, attention is on a domestic AI start-up being described as a "moonshot moment," adding to the ongoing US-China AI competition narrative relevant to the tech complex. On the consumer side, Universal's "The Odyssey" opened at $124.5 million, a data point for the US media and cinema sector.
synthesis:
Today's screen is unambiguous: it's a US value-and-yield harvest, not a growth call. All 10 picks are US-listed, average Value sits at the 88th percentile, Yield at the 90th, and Quality lags visibly at 54 — meaning the machine is paying for cheap cash flow and accepting patchy balance sheets to get it. The composite range is tight (76.4–90.3), and the sector spread is defensive-cyclical barbell: 2 Utilities (ES, EIX), 2 Consumer Defensive (MO, KHC), 2 Consumer Cyclical (BBY, IP), with single names in Tech, Healthcare, Industrials and Materials. Nothing European made the cut despite the EU macro tape.

The clearest thread runs through the dividend names: MO at 5.71%, KHC at 6.18%, IP at 4.93%, ES at 4.22% and EIX at 4.52% all clear the 90th percentile on Yield while trading at double-digit discounts to their sector P/E medians — a classic "buy the payout, question the growth" cluster. The two Utilities deserve a second look given the Thames Water nationalisation fight in the UK: ES and EIX carry debt/equity of 182 and 226 respectively, so any repricing of regulated-utility creditor risk travels. HPQ and BBY form a separate mini-thread — hardware names with 27%+ 3-month returns already banked.

The outlier is CNC: 100th-percentile Value, +73% in three months, but ROE of -26% and no yield — a distressed rerating, not a compounder. The conspicuous gap is Energy: zero picks despite Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure this weekend, alongside no Financials, Real Estate or Communication Services. Watch the Iran escalation and any crude spike — both would rewrite the Utilities and Consumer Defensive theses embedded in this list.
